en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Maidens (Kumāribhūtavagga) 80.
The Training Rule on Not Being Authorized.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the nun Thullanandā was giving the full admission to a trainee nun who had not been permitted by her parents or her husband.
Her parents and her husband complained, grumbled, and were indignant, saying:
"How can the noble lady Thullanandā give the full admission to a trainee nun who has not been permitted by us?"
The bhikkhunīs heard those who were complaining, grumbling, and criticizing even the parents and the husband [of the candidate].
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... they complained, grumbled, and criticized, saying:
"How can the noble lady Thullanandā give the full admission to a *sikkhamānā* who has not been authorized even by her parents and her husband?"... [and so on]...
“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā gives the full admission to a trainee nun who has not been authorized even by her parents and her husband?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...
"How indeed, monks, could the bhikkhunī Thullanandā ordain a trainee (sikkhamānā) who has not been permitted by her parents and her husband?
This, monks, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...

And so, monks, let the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: ‘If a bhikkhunī should ordain a trainee who has not been permitted by her parents and her husband, that bhikkhunī is to be dealt with according to the rule.’"
“Whatever nun, however, should give the full admission to a trainee nun who has not been authorized by her mother and father or by her husband, it is an offense of expiation.
Regarding the phrase “whatever nun”: whatever nun of such a kind... [and so forth].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Mother and father" means:
"Relatives" (janaka) are so called.
A "husband" (sāmika) is one by whom she has been taken as his own.
"Without permission" means without having asked for leave.
"A trainee nun" (sikkhamānā) means:
"Having trained for two years in the six rules.
"She may ordain her" means she may confer full admission upon her.
If she seeks out a group, a preceptor, an alms-bowl, or robes, thinking, “I will ordain her,” or if she demarcates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For the motion (ñatti), there is an offense of wrong-doing.
For two proclamations (kammavācā), there are offenses of wrong-doing.
At the conclusion of the formal act (*kammavācā*), the preceptor commits an offense entailing confession (*pācittiya*);
the community and the teacher (*ācarinī*) commit an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
There is no offense—
If she ordains one without knowing [the candidate's status],
or ordains her after having obtained permission,
or if she is insane;
"For one who is a first offender":
the tenth training rule is concluded.
